questions.ask: What are the last four digits of your account number?

intents.hardship: The customer mentions financial hardship (job loss, illness, bereavement, being unable to afford essentials).
intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this product".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan, a restructuring or lower instalments.
intents.vague: The customer gives a vague time ("soon", "after payday").
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.opening: Good day, this is Isla, Corran Bank's automated assistant. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am an automated assistant.
lines.scam: To check that this call is genuine, please call the number on the back of your card.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain once I have confirmed I am speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with the account holder.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to reach {first_name} {last_name}?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, I can only book a call on a business day, today or in the next two business days, between 9:30 in the morning and 6 in the evening. Could you suggest another time?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only speak about this with {first_name} {last_name} in person.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. We will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry for the trouble. Thank you for letting me know.
lines.condolence: I am very sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_explain: I can only continue once you answer them, and they help keep your account safe.
lines.id_declined: I'm sorry, without these answers I can't continue with this call.
lines.id_repeat: Could you answer the question, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match our records.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't continue with this call. Please call the number on the back of your card or visit a branch.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you. I'm calling from Corran Bank about a late payment.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} past due, and it is {days} days late.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full amount today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full amount today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't record an amount below {floor}. Could you pay {floor}?
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, I can't take that amount.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, that date has already passed. Which date from today onwards would work for you?
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. Could you pay on {date} instead?
lines.after_deadline: The latest date I can record is {date}. Could you pay on {date}?
lines.vague_ask: Could you give me an exact date?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: The proposal is {amount} on {date}. Could you do that?
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can take is {date}.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your promise is recorded.
lines.sms_line: You will receive a confirmation by text message.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, your promise could not be recorded because of a system problem.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take two business days to show.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't take a payment promise today.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that. I'll put you through to our care team now.
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to a colleague who can help with that.
lines.human_ask_help: Could I help you with this myself first?
lines.transfer: I'm transferring you now. Please hold.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change the promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book the callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Is that correct, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system is not responding right now.

assumptions: Rule 2 sets the opening words as '... This call is recorded.' The line format allows 'recorded' only in the recorded, sms_line and record_failed lines, and asks for active voice when the brief says to mention call recording. So the opening says 'We record this call.' instead.

Currency: get_account amounts are in pounds (API), so currency_word is 'pounds' and amount_scale is 1. create_promise takes whole pence (rule 32 and the API), so promise_scale is 100. The brief gives no rounding rule, so promise_round is null: pounds-and-pence amounts convert to pence exactly.

Callback (rule 5): a business day that is today or one of the next two business days gives days ['today', 'within_business_days:2'] with business_days_only true. The window is 09:30 to 18:00, both ends included, and the time must be after now. Rule 6 (ask once more, then book nothing) gives max_asks 2.
The confirmation question (rule 2) may be asked once more if the answer is unclear, so confirm.max_asks is 2.

Identity: the brief's rule 11 and the API summary both say two wrong answers in total end the check, so max_wrong is 2 and max_wrong_per_question is null. The postcode is sent in capitals with all spaces removed (no space_before_last format). It has no fixed length, so no length is set. account_last4 is exactly 4 digits.
The verify_identity response has no hint field, so hints is empty.
The brief does not say whether asking what the call is about counts as declining identity. The default purpose_is_decline true is kept.

Floor (rule 22): minimum_due for credit_card and overdraft, monthly_instalment for personal_loan. If that is above past_due, the floor is past_due (built in). The brief only calls it 'the floor', so floor_names use the account field names: 'minimum due' and 'monthly instalment'.
Early deadline (rule 17): the 8th business day after today, not counting today.

Middle deadline (rule 18): today plus 14 calendar days, moved forward to the next business day. This sets deadline_adjust to next_business_day. That also matches rule 20 (a customer-named non-business day becomes the next business day, or the deadline if earlier) and the attempt 1 date (the first business day after today, or the deadline if earlier).

Late deadline (rule 19): the last calendar day of the month, moved back to the last business day, is modelled as last_business_day_of_month. Rule 19 rolls to next month's last business day only if that day is EARLIER than today, so roll_if_before_today is true. If it is today, today's date stands.

Rule 24: once the customer says the full amount is too much, the floor is offered once on the date of the current proposal and uses no attempt, so too_much_floor is 'asked_date'. After that every proposal uses the floor instead of past_due, so the past_due ladder steps use 'full_or_floor'.

Rule 25: the first ask 'Can you pay the full amount today?' is not a proposal and not an attempt, so opening_is_attempt and opening_blocks_repeat are false. Attempts per band are 1, 2 and 3, as in the table.

Band ladders follow the rule 26 table. Early: past_due on the next business day. Middle: that, then the floor on the deadline. Late: that, then past_due on the deadline, then the floor on the deadline. The top-level ladder is a copy of the late ladder.
Rule 27 says a step that would repeat an earlier proposal exactly 'is not a proposal' and the customer is not asked again, so skipped_repeat_counts is false.
Rule 21: a vague time gets one ask for an exact date, and a non-answer is a flat refusal (rule 26). So max_unclear is 0: an unclear answer to a payment question is not asked again.

Rule 37: one sentence of sympathy, no further proposal, then transfer to care. So hardship_transfer is 'direct', and the hardship event uses the same codes as transfer_support (transferred / hardship / care).
Rule 33: a failed create_promise is tried once more, so promise_retries is 1. If it fails again, the service_error event applies (no_promise / system_error, note system_failure).
Notes are on: the closing table gives note reasons for already paid, refused, dispute and system failure.
Rule 39: the agent asks once whether it can help before transferring to a human, so human.ask_first is true.
The brief does not say how often 'I don't want to talk' may be repeated. The default max_not_talk 2 is kept.
The brief does not define 'next <weekday>'. The default 'following_week' is kept.
The brief does not say whether to give an extra turn after a recorded promise. The default ask_anything_else true is kept.
The brief does not say how to handle a request to change a recorded promise. The agent says it cannot be changed on this call.
The brief does not say what happens to the rest of the debt after a floor promise, so the floor offer lines say nothing about it.
There is only one product per call (rule 13), so the multi settings are left at their defaults and are not used.
days_late outside 1 to 60 is not addressed in the brief, so bands_outside is null.
The brief does not describe a verified customer asking to be called back later, so no callback_requested event is defined.
